item.title: Close to 8,000 plants believed to be marijuana seized in Northern Division raid
item.description: Close to 8,000 plants believed to be marijuana have been seized during a police operation at the Bilobiloca farming area in the Northern Division. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid was made possible through information sharing, with a drone later deployed to confirm the cultivation site.
item.content:encoded:
Close to 8,000 plants believed to be marijuana have been seized during a police operation at the Bilobiloca farming area in the Northern Division.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid was made possible through information sharing, with a drone later deployed to confirm the cultivation site.

Vusonilawe says community support has been instrumental in the success of such raids, leading to seizures and arrests.

He says the sharing of information reflects the community's support for law enforcement efforts , and the Fiji Police Force extends its appreciation for the continued support towards crime prevention efforts.

The Assistant Commissioner says drug operations are multifaceted, with officers not only targeting illicit drugs but also other offences to ensure a holistic approach to tackling crime.

Police are urging members of the public to call 1681 to report crimes, share information or raise concerns about service delivery.

item.title: Police verifying claims of alleged attempted child abduction at Nausori school
item.description: Police are verifying claims made on social media of an alleged attempted child abduction at a school in Nausori after a post identified a man who has since denied the allegation and told Police he had gone to the school to see his daughter. Following the circulation of the social media post, Nausori Police carried out initial enquiries and confirmed that the matter remains under investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Police are verifying claims made on social media of an alleged attempted child abduction at a school in Nausori after a post identified a man who has since denied the allegation and told Police he had gone to the school to see his daughter.

Following the circulation of the social media post, Nausori Police carried out initial enquiries and confirmed that the matter remains under investigation.

Police have also confirmed that the man identified in the post has lodged a report at the Lami Police Station.

He told Police that he had gone to the school to see his daughter, not for the reasons claimed in the social media post.

The man says he only became aware of the allegations after family members alerted him when they saw the post online, prompting him to report the matter to Police.

Police say investigations are continuing to establish the facts, with more people expected to be questioned.

They are urging members of the public to report incidents directly to Police and allow investigators to carry out their work before drawing conclusions.

Police are also reminding the public that the 1681 toll-free number can be used to report crimes, suspicious people or activities, as well as complaints against Police and concerns about service delivery.

item.title: Charan Jeath Singh returns as Sugar Minister
item.description: Charan Jeath Singh has returned as Sugar Minister after Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka reversed an earlier Cabinet allocation that placed responsibility for the portfolio under Agriculture Minister Tomasi Tunabuna. Singh says he was informed of the decision in an email from the Prime Minister on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
Charan Jeath Singh has returned as Sugar Minister after Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka reversed an earlier Cabinet allocation that placed responsibility for the portfolio under Agriculture Minister Tomasi Tunabuna.

Singh says he was informed of the decision in an email from the Prime Minister on Monday night.

While speaking to fijivillage News, Singh says he will continue the work he had started in the sugar industry and ensure it moves forward.

The Minister has thanked the Prime Minister for restoring the Sugar portfolio to him.

He is expected to formally take up the portfolio next week.

item.title: MSAF reminds skippers to comply with Maritime safety rules
item.description: As Fiji enters a busy season of inter-island travel and commercial maritime activity the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) is reminding all small boat owners, resort transport managers, and commercial vessel operators to comply with the Maritime Transport Act. item.content:encoded:
As Fiji enters a busy season of inter-island travel and commercial maritime activity the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) is reminding all small boat owners, resort transport managers, and commercial vessel operators to comply with the Maritime Transport Act.

MSAF says every skipper must operate strictly within the limitations stated on their MSAF Certificate of Competency to help protect lives, passengers, and vessels operating in Fiji's waters.

The Authority says holders of a Boat Master Licence (BML) are authorised to operate vessels that are less than 15 metres in length and under 20 Gross Registered Tonnage (GRT) only within sheltered waters, including rivers, harbours, bays, and protected inner reefs.

They say additional endorsements are required before BML holders can undertake open-ocean passages or outer-island voyages.

MSAF also says holders of a Restricted Master/Engineer Class 6 (RME-6) certificate are restricted to operating vessels under 15 metres and 20 GRT on designated inshore voyages.

These operators are responsible for both the safe navigation of the vessel and ensuring t he engine is in proper working order, with machinery and bilge checks expected to be completed before every departure.

The Authority is reminding boat owners, employers, and vessel managers that they are responsible for ensuring crew members hold the appropriate qualifications for the size of the vessel they are operating and the intended voyage area before departure.

MSAF is encouraging maritime employers and resort operators to review their crew certifications and vessel survey documents, saying that safe seas depend on shared responsibility and strict compliance with maritime safety requirements.
